threat_internal_label: people using AI to fabricate breaking news (never shown on screen)
analog: Fake AI-generated image of an 'explosion near the Pentagon', shared by paid-verified accounts on May 22, 2023; brief US stock-market dip
actors_note: The red is people's choices: someone generated a fake photo and posted it as news, and accounts posing as news outlets (one impersonating a financial news brand) chose to amplify it without checking. The image tool is not the actor. On screen, a human hand types the prompt and presses 'post'.
t0: 2023-05-22 08:42 ET, first known share of the image on Twitter (per NPR). Other outlets say the first share was 'just after 9 a.m.' by a different account; the first-post time is contested.

sources.title: NPR: Fake viral images of an explosion at the Pentagon were probably created by AI (May 22, 2023) - first share by @CBKNews121 at 8:42 a.m. ET; Arlington fire department tweet around 10:27 a.m. ET

AP FACT FOCUS: Fake image of Pentagon explosion briefly sends jitters through stock market (May 22, 2023) - Dow fell ~80 points 10:06-10:10, recovered by 10:13; S&P 500 from +0.02% at 10:06 to -0.15% at 10:09, positive again by 10:11
ABC News: How verified accounts helped make fake images of a Pentagon explosion go viral (May 2023) - 8:42 a.m. share; Cyabra found ~3,785 accounts mentioned the falsehood, dozens verified

Al Jazeera: Fake Pentagon explosion photo goes viral: How to spot an AI image (May 23, 2023) - first shared by OSINTdefender 'just after 9 a.m.'; 'Bloomberg Feed' (650,000+ followers) posted at 10:06 a.m.; Bellingcat's Nick Waters flagged flaws

CNN Business: 'Verified' Twitter accounts share fake image of 'explosion' near Pentagon, causing confusion (May 22, 2023) - RT (3M+ followers) shared then deleted; Arlington County Fire Department statement
WUNC/NPR syndication: Nick Waters (Bellingcat) tweeted he was confident the image was AI-generated, citing the fence melding into barriers and no first-hand witness posts
Bloomberg: Fake AI Photo of Pentagon Blast Goes Viral and Trips Stocks Briefly (May 22, 2023)
TheStreet: S&P Sheds $500 Billion from Fake Pentagon Explosion (headline only seen; not checked)

points.event: 08:42 ET first known share of the fabricated image
10:06 ET: account posing as a financial news feed posts it (s4); S&P 500 at +0.02%
points.notes: extent 0.1 is a drawing aid for 'reaching the market', not a measured share

points.event: 10:09 ET: S&P 500 at -0.15%, the low of the dip

events.event: 'just after 9 a.m.' an OSINT-branded account shares it (s4 calls this the original share; conflicts with s1)
10:11 ET: S&P 500 positive again (Dow recovered by 10:13, t=91)
~10:27 ET: Arlington County Fire Department: no explosion or incident at or near the Pentagon

threat.notes: extent = fraction of the peak market reaction (S&P 500 move from +0.02% to -0.15%, i.e. 0.17 percentage points in 3 minutes), the only time-resolved measure of the red's reach found. Total spread: ~3,785 accounts mentioned it (Cyabra via s3), but no time series or window was given, so no doubling time. Media reported a ~$500B paper swing in S&P market value (s8, headline only); not independently checked, don't show. The fire department's statement at t=105 came after the market had already self-corrected at t=89.

fragments.who: Arlington County Fire Department and Pentagon Force Protection Agency
fragments.had: the ground truth: nothing had happened
fragments.notes: the truth existed on the ground from t0; the public statement came at ~t=105 (s1)

fragments.had: the verification skill: spotted the melting fence and the absence of any eyewitness photos from a busy location
fragments.notes: the exact time of the debunking post was not found; it was the same morning

fragments.who: people nearby and traders who checked for corroboration
fragments.had: the missing second source: no one on the ground saw anything
fragments.notes: the market recovered within ~3-5 minutes of the dip, before any official statement

fragments.had: the visual tells (e.g. a streetlamp both in front of and behind a barrier; a building that doesn't match)
fragments.notes: analysis published later the same day; hour not found

aggregation.notes: Derived from documented moments after t0, not a measured distribution: p10 = market self-corrects at 10:11 ET (t=89, s2); median = official 'no explosion' statement ~10:27 ET (t=105, s1); p90 = AP's published fact check, ~17:22 ET (t=520), read from the timestamp embedded in the AP/Yahoo URL (212249 = 21:22:49 UTC), verified: false. The debunk arrived ~21 minutes after the market hit, but ~105 minutes after the first post, while the people who knew the truth (f1) had it from t0.

deploy.notes: The official statement is the deployment: once public it ended the confusion. RT deleted its post; the impersonating account was suspended (times not found).

ai_counterfactual.basis: Illustrative. Here one person used an image generator to fabricate news; the counterfactual is other people using AI to check it. Two steps, both short: (1) for a claimed explosion in a busy, heavily photographed location, check whether any independent eyewitness posts, images or scanner reports exist (the test the open-source investigator applied by hand), and (2) route the rising claim to the local authority that holds the ground truth (f1) so they can confirm in public. Each is a minutes-scale task, far inside the ~17.4 h 50% task horizon in RATES.md (METR entry), and RATES.md's falling cost at fixed capability (~40x/yr, Epoch) makes screening every fast-rising breaking-news claim affordable. Assumed ~30 min from first post to a routed question to the fire department, i.e. before the 10:06 amplification. Deliberately NOT based on pixel-level 'AI image detection', which is unreliable; it relies on corroboration and routing. People still confirm and publish. Not a claim the dip would certainly have been avoided.
ai_counterfactual.label: illustrative

gap_summary: One person's fabricated photo sat for ~84 min, then moved the market in 3 min; people on the ground knew the truth from minute 0, but the official 'nothing happened' landed at ~105 min, after traders had already corrected on their own.
